newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Pharmos drug moves to phase II trial.
newsitem.headline: Pharmos drug moves to phase II trial.

text.p: Pharmos Corp said on Wednesday it had received Israeli Health Ministry approval to begin the phase II study of its proprietary neurological drug Dexanabinol.

Pharmos, a Florida-based company that conducts most of its operations in Israel, also announced completion of a $2 million private placement with U.S. institutional investors of preferred stock convertible to common shares.

Dexanabinol is being developed to treat neurological damage caused by stroke, head and spinal cord injuries. The phase II study, which should take about one year, will be conducted at six Israeli medical centres.

Michael Schikler, vice president for Israel operations, said the company hoped to complete all trials and win U.S. Food and Drug Adminstration approval in about four years. Although several companies are developing similar treatments to date, he said, no drug has yet been approved for these applications.
He estimated the worldwide market at 1.5 million cases annually, with an average cost per treatment of at least $1,000.

Pharmos as yet has no commercial products but does have a drug, called Lotemax, for treating occular inflammation under FDA review. If approved, Lotemax will be produced and marketed in the U.S., and perhaps elsewhere, by Bausch & Lomb, Schikler said.
No strategic partnership for Dexanabinol has yet been formed, he said.
